threads.title: WeightTraining #158
threads.preview:
That is what I want to hear. Lock it in.

Quick checklist before you touch a bar

paragraphs: Look, you said you were going to get back on the board with a lift, and you got 23 minutes in yesterday morning. It breaks the dry spell. Let me know what you actually hit in that session, what the RPE was, and if we're still locking in another lift this weekend.

messages.text: That was just morning foundation coach

paragraphs: Got it. So that was foundation, not the lift. Which means the dry spell is still live, Sky. You committed to getting one real lift in this weekend before the travel window hits next week. Are we locking in Workout A today or tomorrow?

messages.text: I will do it today coach!

paragraphs:
That is what I want to hear. Lock it in.

Quick checklist before you touch a bar:
1. Single-leg glute bridge on the right in the warm-up. Squeeze before extending.
2. Front lever protocol: SL FL benchmark tested LEFT first, then straddle negatives (25kg band, 5x3 controlled), then SL holds (15kg band, 3x10s).
3. Dips stay at bodyweight with that 3-second eccentric.

Keep it clean, get your numbers down, and tell me how it felt when you're done.

input.message: Can you build me a new bodyweight strength routine I can do at home, no equipment, three times a week?

output.reply: Look, if we're doing this at home with zero gear, it has to be crisp and intentional, not just going through motions. I put together 'Bodyweight Strength at Home' for you. Warm-up hits your right glute activation first with single-leg bridges so that hip stays awake. Main work pairs push-ups, bodyweight Bulgarian split squats, pike push-ups for vertical pressing, and single-leg RDLs, wrapped up with hard tension planks. Three rounds, clean quality over rushing. Take a look and let me know how it fits.

Take a look and let me know how it fits.

I pulled that home routine right off your board, so you have a clean slate. When you get in there and see what kit they have, give me the rundown and we will map out a real plan.

messages.text: Can you build me a new bodyweight strength routine I can do at home, no equipment, three times a week?

paragraphs: Look, if we're doing this at home with zero gear, it has to be crisp and intentional, not just going through motions. I put together 'Bodyweight Strength at Home' for you. Warm-up hits your right glute activation first with single-leg bridges so that hip stays awake. Main work pairs push-ups, bodyweight Bulgarian split squats, pike push-ups for vertical pressing, and single-leg RDLs, wrapped up with hard tension planks. Three rounds, clean quality over rushing. Take a look and let me know how it fits.

messages.text: Actually, on second thought, remove that routine you just made - I've decided to join a gym instead and want a clean slate.

paragraphs: Look, I respect that. Joining a gym gives us way more tools to load the movement patterns properly and keep your strength progressing without having to force unnatural bodyweight angles. I pulled that home routine right off your board, so you have a clean slate. When you get in there and see what kit they have, give me the rundown and we will map out a real plan.

input.message: That's it for today, wrap this up.

output.reply: Look, get after your weekend. When you check out the gym, drop me a note with the equipment they have and we'll build the plan around it. Rest up.
